title: Dialogue-skew-aware time-slice batcher and KV compaction
creator: Asha Mehta
description:
Background: In mixed prompt/response length workloads (chatbots, multi-turn helpers) we observe high tail latency and GPU memory fragmentation. Long responses hold large KV caches and long-running stream slots, starving short requests and increasing eviction churn. Current length-priority binning reduces some head-of-line blocking but still causes high P99 for short prompts and elevated peak GPU memory.

Proposal: Implement a dialogue-skew-aware time-slice batching policy plus an aggressive KV compaction tier. The scheduler will: 1) partition long-response generation into configurable time-slices (max tokens or wall-time) so long streams yield execution slices allowing short requests to be interleaved; 2) use a lightweight response-length predictor at enqueue time (tokenizer-based & early-step estimator) to set slice aggressiveness; 3) introduce a KV compaction pass that identifies cold KV entries and either compresses or offloads them to host memory with fast warm-up path; 4) add per-GPU memory watermarks and preemptive packing rules that favor packing many short dialogs into micro-batches between slices.

Trade-offs: Slicing can add scheduling overhead and slight per-token latency but reduces P99 for short requests and lowers peak resident memory. Compaction introduces CPU/GPU transfer work; need to bound compaction to low-util periods or background worker threads.

Goals: Reduce short-request P99 by >=25% under mixed workloads, decrease peak GPU memory by >=15%, and lower KV eviction rate by >=30% without increasing average token cost by more than 5%.
steps: Instrument current scheduler to capture sliceable long-response traces and KV lifetimes (runtime metrics + flamegraphs)
Implement lightweight response-length predictor and feature gate (runtime + SDK opt-in flag)
Add time-slice scheduling primitive to continuous-batcher (configurable tokens and wall-time limits)
Implement KV compaction tier: compress cold KV blocks and host-offload with fast restore path
Introduce GPU watermark thresholds and preemptive packing heuristics in allocator
Write unit/integration tests and synthetic workload harness for mixed-length dialog profiles
Canary rollout on dedicated test pool and run A/B load tests against stable scheduler
Collect metrics, iterate on slice sizes and compaction thresholds, and finalize rollout plan
acceptance_criteria: Config flag gated: toggle time-slice policy per-model without restart
A/B tests show >=25% P99 reduction for short-turn queries on mixed workloads
Peak GPU resident memory reduced by >=15% in synthetic replay of production traffic
KV eviction rate decreases by >=30% and cache warm-up fast path < 50ms median
No degradation of median token latency by more than 5% versus baseline
Dashboard: per-model per-customer SLO charts and compaction exported metrics available
Production canary running for 72h with automated rollback on error budget violation
comments: 2025-07-08 Asha Mehta: Initial triage - captured high P99 on production mixed-dialog workload. Created hypothesis that slicing + compaction reduces head-of-line blocking and memory churn.
2025-07-10 Diego Ruiz: Design draft uploaded. Note: need to verify cost of host-offload path for 80-series GPUs; flagged for infra review.
2025-07-14 Infra review (Rajat Patel): Host-offload acceptable if compaction is background-limited and bounded; recommend cap at 10% CPU budget per GPU.
2025-07-16 Design review: PM (Lina Chen) requested per-customer SLO weighting and opt-out flag. Added feature gate in plan.
2025-07-20 Diego Ruiz: Implemented prototype time-slice primitive and added unit tests. PR opened: runtime#8172. Initial synthetic run shows P99 short-request improvement ~18% with slice=100ms.

2025-07-22 Perf notes: With KV compaction enabled in prototype, peak GPU memory down ~12% and eviction rate down ~22%; still short of targets but promising. Next: tune slice size and compaction thresholds and add host-offload warmup cache.
2025-07-22 QA: Added synthetic fuzz tests for long-hallucination streams to ensure slicing doesn't starve long responses; found small reconstruction bug fixed in runtime#8185
